full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Matin J: These petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the judgment and order dated 24.04.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 3427, 3388, 3391 and 3389 of 1997 making the Rule absolute arising out of the judgment and decree dated 27.11.1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court. Feni allowing the Title Appeal No. 30 of 1992 and reversing the judgment and decree dated 01.03.1992 passed by the learned Upazila Assistant Judge, Dagunbhuiyan in decreeing the Title Suit No. 59 of 1989. 

 4. It was stated that the respondent and other 3 more persons being plaintiffs instituted four Title Suit being No. 26 of 1990, 27 of 1990, 590 of 1989 and 60 of 1989 and all the suits were heard analogously and were decreed. Then four title appeals were preferred being Nos. 23 of 1992, 24 of 1992, 30 of 1992 and 31 of 1992 which were also heard analogously and all the appeals were allowed by the same judgment. 

 5. Both the parties adduced witnesses and exhibited documents to prove their respective cases and upon hearing the parties the learned Assistant Judge was pleased to decree the suit against which the defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 31 of 1992 and upon hearing the learned appellate court was pleased to allow the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 17.11.1997. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 17.11.1997 passed by the then learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Feni plaintiff preferred the Civil Revision No. 3388 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule and the Rule has been numbered   as Civil Revision No. 3427 of 1997. 

 10. It appears that the High Court Division believed the contract and found that the plaintiff was entitled to get the kabala in question and the trial court rightly decreed the suit since the contract has been believed the suit should have been decreed by the appellate court.
